Q: Volatile Variable Coherence A:

Duplicate of When to use volatile with multi threading? - on real implementations such as GCC / Clang / MSVC, volatile is similar for std::atomic with std::memory_order_relaxed, for types small enough to be lock-free without special instructions on the target machine.

You of course don't get atomic RMWs for i++, but you do get atomic store and load. (As an implementation-specific guarantee. The ISO C++ standard leaves the behaviour undefined.)

But don't roll your own atomics; if volatile compiles to the asm you want, you could have gotten the same thing in a well-defined way with std::atomic. The bad old days before C++11 are long ago, so only a very few longstanding code-bases use volatile (and inline asm memory barriers) to roll their own, such at the Linux kernel.

Treating these as relaxed loads/stores like they would be across threads on x86 or ARM, I don't see an execution / memory ordering that would lead to neither being printed, not even in the C++ abstract machine let alone in real cache-coherent machines.

StoreLoad reordering can't happen in the normal sense because it's the same variable being stored and loaded: even relaxed has coherence rules. The reload can happen before the store is globally visible, thanks to store forwarding. So a thread can see its own stores before they become globally visible. On machines that aren't other-multi-copy-atomic, it's also possible for a store to become visible to some threads before all threads. (This can happen on PowerPC, and maybe some NVidia ARMv7 chips, but not ARMv8 or x86). But again that's not relevant here.

Both stores will become part of the modification-order of i (according to the order of threads gaining MESI exclusive ownership and committing their store). Each load will read from some point in the modification-order after the store in the same thread, so it might see its own store or the one from the other thread. But they can't both see the store from the other thread. One thread's store goes first, and that thread's load might see it or the other value. But the other thread's store goes second, so it will definitely be the value seen by that thread's load.

Q: How to change gui font size in JavaFX SceneBuilder? A:

I don't like editing a jar file. Linux probably overwrites this jar on update without notice. In theory the solution should be:

  • Copy the CSS file out of the jar, keeping the relative path

  • rename it to "MyTheme"

  • edit as you need

  • add the path where you put it into your classpath
